dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: We're counting on you to wrap this match up fast... But this challenge's a little different, so keep your guard up.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Easy there. No need to go all out and bring the whole Domain down.

choices.text: What are you doing between matches?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: I'm treating Iris to a couple drinks. She got me these sunglasses in Fontaine, so I owe her.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: I'll be in Snezhnaya for a while, so I'd better get used to warming up with the local Fire-Water. I'm taking a quick break first.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: I should ask Iris for tips, too. She's been on Dragonspine for years. She probably knows enough about handling the cold to write a whole book series.

choices.text: I never really thought about commission ranks before.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: No need to think too hard about it. It's just a rough way to describe what kind of commissions an adventurer can handle alone.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: I'm guessing you want to know where the commissions we usually give you fall, right?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: A hilichurl outpost raid is a good example. Adventurers call those "Increasing Danger," and they're usually treated as B-rank commissions.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: For that kind of job, the Guild recommends at least sixteen regular adventurers and warriors, with no fewer than six solid marksmen.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: The usual plan is to have six people keep any Mitachurls in the outpost busy, while four handle the regular hilichurls.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: The six marksmen take out the Hilichurl Crossbowmen on the towers first, then help wear down the Mitachurls. Once they're down, the whole party moves in to clear the camp.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: That can take three to five hours, so it's more about endurance than brute force.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: If possible, bring a cook with the party so everyone can recover after the fight and be ready if hilichurl reinforcements show up.

choices.text: It doesn't seem that complicated to me...

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Right, and that's why you shouldn't get too hung up on the rating. By today's standards, it's pretty broad.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Iris's said the same thing before. A B-rank hilichurl camp in Dragonspine and a B-rank "Increasing Danger" commission in a normal area aren't really the same at all.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: We're suggesting that each rank should also have a difficulty score. For example, B-rank would be 601 to 700 points. That way, adventurers can get a better idea of how hard a commission is before they take it.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: There'll be a meeting about it after the event ends, so you'll hear more then.

choices.text: I usually just go in and get it done...
I heard something about adventurer ranks this time.
I've fought my way through enough by now. I'm not scared.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Heh, fair enough. A fight on paper's still a fight. Go on, then. Let's see what you've got, all-rounder.
